references.text: A parallel law in Deuteronomy that repeats the same criteria for clean animals: split hooves and chewing the cud.
The following verses elaborate on the prohibition by mentioning specific examples of animals that meet only one of the criteria.
Ezekiel refers to the distinction between clean and unclean in connection with temple service and laws of holiness.
Peter's vision where God declares all animals clean, illustrating the new covenant's relationship to Old Testament dietary rules.
Peter recounts the vision about clean and unclean animals, and how God abolished the distinction between clean and unclean.
